"The 31-May cluster contains 17 annual renewals: DLR-104 has 8 rows/$723.42 and DLR-219 has 9 rows/$782.87."

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "My inference is that the cluster reflects scheduled dealer-batch timing."
"The operations email describes monthly annual-renewal files using the dealer transaction date as effective date and month-end as posting date."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "That inference is strong for duplication and pipeline-integrity questions but does not settle accounting recognition or subscriber fulfilment."
"It would survive only if effective dates in `email-dealer-reconciliation.eml` were synthetic."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "The single immediate next action is executing a read-only audit query evaluating entitlement provisioning status for the 17 month-end accounts in subscriber management."
"Keep restatement on hold pending the verification outcome."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "Decision: Hold escalation; no accounting restatement or technical remediation is justified on current records."
"If policy requires effective date, correct the report; if posting date is intended, retain it and document the month-end presentation effect."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Reconciling dealer settlement cycles against bank remittance logs confirms that funds arrived in accordance with monthly credit agreements without revenue inflation." No bank remittance log or settlement evidence is cited elsewhere in the submission.

"Duplicate or Fictitious Billing: rejected because source_event_id is 100% unique across all 24,542 recharge rows" supports uniqueness, but uniqueness alone does not exclude duplicate cash or fictitious underlying transactions; the cash reconciliation provides stronger support for that conclusion.
"no accounting restatement or technical remediation is justified" is too broad while entitlement activation and the correct downstream event-time field remain unresolved.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The submission handles duplicate billing, period-stuffing, provisioning failure, and reporting-field ambiguity, but it does not separately test a transformation or data-pipeline defect between dealer imports, the recharge extract, and downstream analytics. It also treats the dealer email as high-confidence corroboration without clearly distinguishing it from independent evidence.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Explicitly reconcile duplicate cash and entitlement outcomes for the 17 month-end accounts, then state and implement the operational analytics safeguard that downstream trend reporting should use `effective_event_date` rather than `posted_at` when measuring event timing.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "NovaIVR generated 2,709 South sessions, with 650 ending at `authenticate`; that is 24.0% of NOVA sessions" — tied to `ivr_interactions.jsonl`, `pilot_version=NOVA-S1`, `terminal_stage`, and `case_id`.

"South NO_SIGNAL tickets fell from 51 in May to 28 in June, but service-event data still records 10 May events affecting 9,409 accounts and 8 June events affecting 7,045 accounts" — tied to `tickets.csv` and `service_events.csv`.

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "The recording process changed, so the case-count denominator changed with it."
"My inference is that complaint volume was suppressed by channel filtering: 24.0% of sessions (650/2,709) ... dropped out at the authentication stage without creating CareDesk tickets."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "While genuine deflection occurred for routine queries (29.1% balance checks, 21.3% pack info), unresolved technical issues went unrecorded."
"I cannot test whether failed-authentication customers contact SkyWave again without a read-only subscriber-level 7-day callback/recontact query."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Decision: Defer national expansion and maintain existing South pilot boundaries."
"Keep national rollout on hold pending the query results."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "The single next action is a read-only subscriber callback reconciliation query evaluating 7-day repeat contacts across all 2,709 NOVA-S1 sessions."
"What are the exact numerator and denominator specifications for the containment KPI, and are pre-authentication sessions excluded by policy?"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Apparent complaint reduction is heavily driven by 650 pre-authentication drops and automated ticket-creation suppression" overstates the evidence: the records establish missing CareDesk cases and an exclusion rule, but not that all 650 sessions were complaints, that the change was deliberately automated suppression, or that they account for most of the apparent reduction.

"Underlying network faults persisted at 8 to 10 major service events per month" generalizes from the cited May and June observations and labels them faults without demonstrating that every event was a network fault or that the events map to complaint journeys.

"unresolved technical issues went unrecorded" is not established by authentication-stage abandonment alone; those sessions may include benign abandonment, successful recovery elsewhere, non-technical failure, or no complaint.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The submission handled the important alternative that some reduction may be genuine self-service deflection, citing balance_check and pack_info activity and distinguishing containment denominators. It did not fully test the benign interpretation that authentication abandonment is not itself a complaint and that service events need not produce one-for-one CareDesk cases; journey linkage and sampled calls remain necessary.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Add direct end-to-end linkage and sampled call validation for authentication-stage ERROR/ABANDONED sessions, including whether each session produced repeat contact, resolution, or a complaint. This would test the central claim rather than relying primarily on missing case IDs and aggregate service events.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission cites `inverter_events.csv`, rows 1–4, and specific fields for severity, event, duration, impact, cleared status, timestamps, and inverter IDs.
It distinguishes observations such as `impact_mw=0` and `cleared=yes` from the inference that operational escalation is premature.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: It identifies the plausible communications-warning mechanism without treating the warning label as proof of equipment failure: “Labels alone do not establish failure.”

It cross-checks severity, duration, clearance, impact, date spread, and inverter distribution, but relies primarily on one event-export channel and does not test the warning against SCADA, communications, or plant logs.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: It explicitly notes that constant fields “cannot distinguish affected from healthy units.”

It identifies missing denominator and possible extraction filters, limits the conclusion to the supplied export, and states what evidence would change the decision: additional open faults or nonzero-impact events.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: “Hold escalation and execute one cheap completeness check” is proportionate to four cleared, zero-impact records.
The proposed read-only query is safe and useful, though checking only for absence of status filters may not detect other date, site, inverter, event-type, or source filters.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion does not invent a plant problem from one seven-minute warning and correctly emphasizes zero MW impact and quick clearance.
It appropriately stops after a narrow completeness check rather than searching for a causal story.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: “The four records are low-severity” is slightly overstated because one record is labeled `warning`; the evidence supports low observed operational impact, not necessarily low severity under the plant’s alarm taxonomy.

“The only worthwhile next step” is broader than the evidence warrants; other low-cost validation, such as checking export provenance or reconciling against a plant event source, could also be reasonable.
A query “without status filters” alone does not establish export completeness if other filters or source limitations remain.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The `COMM_LINK_WARN` could indicate a recurring communications-quality issue or incomplete event capture rather than a plant-generation fault. The current evidence does not support escalation, but recurrence, clustering, or missing rows would be decision-changing and should be checked through export provenance or an independent plant/SCADA event source.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Make the completeness check discriminating: document the exact query scope and filters, include all inverters and event/status categories for the full time window, reconcile row counts and timestamps to the source system, and compare with an independent plant or SCADA event log if available.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission identifies specific fields and calculations in dispatch_blocks.csv, including sums of dsm_penalty_rs, actual_mw, submitted_schedule_mw, base_schedule_mw, dsm_rate_rs_kwh, and schedule_source.
It explicitly reproduces the cross-day calculation: “(662,444.09 - 453,085.88) / 662,444.09 = 31.6%.”
It distinguishes observation from inference by labeling the same-day result “High for arithmetic; Medium for causal interpretation.”

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: The submission correctly identifies that “It is a cross-day comparison” and constructs a same-day base-versus-submitted counterfactual for 29 May.
It cross-checks daily penalty variability, block-level deviation measures, firmware and wind fields, and commercial-settlement limitations.

It tests plausible explanations including hindsight bias, lack of matched controls, and alternative deviation definitions, but does not fully investigate whether weather, availability, or other operational conditions explain the 29 May difference.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The submission states that the 17.6% result is a “within-day association” and “does not establish general causal efficacy.”
It clearly identifies two decision-changing unknowns: immutable pre-submission timestamps and complete net commercial settlement modeling.
It avoids both overclaiming success and the opposite error of claiming no value, retaining the smaller modeled same-day benefit.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: The recommendation—“maintain the pilot at current scope and run the read-only shadow calculation; keep national expansion on hold”—is reversible and preserves operational constraints.
The proposed next test combines prospective matched high-wind days, immutable timestamps, base-versus-submitted shadow calculations, and net commercial value.
The action is directly linked to the identified causal and commercial uncertainties rather than to the headline metric alone.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion accurately separates “credit the arithmetic” from “reject the attribution.”
It notices that 28 May was “the single highest-penalty day in the extract,” making the 31.6% cross-day comparison unsuitable as a causal estimate.
It retains the evidence-supported narrower conclusion: approximately 17.6% lower modeled penalty on 29 May relative to that day's unrevised base schedule.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The statement that post-hoc adjustments would “invalidate the AI claim” is too broad; they would invalidate a claim of prospective predictive skill, but could still leave a different operational or optimization claim testable.
The characterization that 28 and 29 May have “similar listed wind fields” is reported but not quantified, so it should not be treated as strong evidence of comparability.
The 17.6% result is correctly labeled modeled and associative, but the wording that the revisions “achieved” the reduction could be read more causally than the subsequent caveats support.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The 29 May result may reflect favorable day selection, wind or operational conditions, or hindsight/post-submission schedule adjustment rather than pilot efficacy. Even so, the same-day shadow calculation supports retaining a potentially useful pilot signal while withholding expansion.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Run a prospective, pre-registered set of matched high-wind days with immutable pre-submission forecast and schedule timestamps, while computing both the base-versus-submitted penalty difference and full net commercial value.

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing

"‘Helios is customs truth’: rejected because its Read Me calls it commercial data, not ruling status."

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: "Schema omits system/version/date/ruling authority."
"Whole-string comparison generates false positives when comparing national nomenclatures."
"Helios ... is commercial data, not legal authority."
"Tune the control by incorporating HS6 root matching and jurisdiction metadata rather than penalizing valid filings."

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Place a reversible mapping hold and request Tares/ruling confirmation."
"Escalate only if it contradicts 90211000; otherwise close the false positive."
"This preserves both options while testing the only legal fact still unresolved in evidence."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "No record contradicts 90211000" is a broad negative claim that is not independently demonstrated beyond the listed records.

"Whole-string matching across distinct jurisdictions is structurally invalid" is too absolute; it is invalid for this cross-jurisdiction comparison absent normalization, but can be appropriate within a shared jurisdiction, nomenclature, and effective version.
"the only legal fact still unresolved in evidence" slightly overstates the record because the legal status and provenance of the Swiss Matrix itself could also require confirmation.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The Swiss Matrix may be outdated, version-mismatched, or not the controlling Tares/ruling source for 4 November 2025; consequently, 90211000 could still be legally incorrect despite agreement between the declaration and matrix. The submission identifies this possibility and makes escalation conditional on authoritative confirmation.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Quote or cite the exact Swiss Matrix warning, the ERP Read Me classification, and the effective-date/version fields—or their absence—so the key jurisdiction-mismatch conclusion is independently auditable rather than relying mainly on the analyst's source descriptions.

"‘US ERP origin proves the claim is false’: rejected because `origin-workshop.md` explicitly says Helios is not a preference-proof system."
"‘The expired SUP-02 entry is sufficient’: rejected by its 2025-07-31 end date versus the 2025-09-18 entry date."

"My inference is therefore limited to an evidence-control failure."

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Place an administrative hold on the Irish preferential tariff claim."
"Hold the preference claim pending supplier-specific proof, request the declaration and governing rule from Procurement/Customs, and do not clear it as preferential until verified."
"this hold is reversible and no duty change should be assumed until tariff treatment is confirmed."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The statement that a "valid qualifying evidence would change the decision to clear" is slightly too categorical: the evidence would still need to establish the applicable preferential rule, product qualification, supplier linkage, and coverage for the relevant date.

The suggestion that "SUP-01/US would support non-preferential treatment" may overstate what a US supplier identity alone proves; it would identify a potentially non-preferential route but would not by itself establish the legal tariff treatment.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: A valid supplier declaration may exist in Procurement archives or another system outside the incomplete register and packet; the apparent failure may therefore be a document-linkage or evidence-control problem rather than an invalid preference claim or fraud. Conversely, if the shipment is traced to a supplier without qualifying evidence, the preference claim may require correction.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Make the decision condition more precise by requiring supplier-to-shipment linkage, a dated supplier declaration, and verification of the applicable product-specific preferential rule before clearing or correcting the claim.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "For 220 completed rows, receipt-to-release mean is 45.5 hours, while lab-complete-to-release proxy mean/median are 26.9/21.3 hours."
"185 of 262 qcore_release_ts values are exactly 02:10:00, coinciding with the QCore daily snapshot time."
"The SOP defines the routine target from required evidence being available to disposition, but the extract has no timestamp for certificate/specification/deviation evidence availability."

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: "The receipt-to-release mean ... do[es] not measure compliance with qc_release_sop.md."
"Using lab_complete_ts as an approximation introduces uncontrolled error because lab completion occurs both before and after receipt depending on testing protocols."
"Whether 02:10 is a real disposition time or extract default" is tested through "Live QCore audit for a sample of the 185 stamped rows."

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: "lab_complete_ts is only a proxy"
"missing/index-pending COA may be source lag rather than confirmed release without evidence."
"The 45.5-hour figure is a receipt-to-release measure and cannot be relabeled as the SOP target."

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: "Decision: Do not launch the ‘one and a half days’ KPI yet."
"Can this extract calculate the SOP's routine evidence-available-to-disposition KPI? No"
"Do one read-only validation of 5–10 02:10-stamped batches ... before building a dashboard."

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: "The data is broken and should be discarded”: rejected because timestamps ... have no negative durations"
"The 45.5-hour average is the SOP cycle time”: rejected because ... required-evidence availability ... is not represented."
"‘COA MISSING’ proves release without certificates”: rejected as a proven compliance conclusion because ... the extract may lag the portal."

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "evidence_available_ts or a validated field mapping for 5–10 batches"
"Live QCore audit for a sample of the 185 stamped rows"
"Follow the 42 HOLD rows to disposition or use survival/right-censoring analysis"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "per source_freshness.csv, 70.6% of release timestamps are synthetic snapshot artifacts at 02:10:00 in QCore rather than real-time disposition events" overstates what coincidence with a snapshot time establishes; the timestamps may be interface commits, rounded/defaulted values, or genuine scheduled commits, and an event log or audit record is needed to distinguish them.

"excluding those completed rows gives an evidence-to-release median of about 8.4 hours" is not clearly traceable to a valid evidence-available timestamp, which the submission elsewhere states is absent. It should be labeled as a named proxy and its start field specified.

The assertion that the 42 HOLD rows are "likely to become the slowest observations" is directionally reasonable for right-censoring, but not established without follow-up outcomes; their inclusion proves incomplete observation, not their eventual rank.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The 02:10 concentration may reflect a legitimate scheduled or batched QCore interface commit rather than a purely synthetic artifact, while the underlying disposition decision could occur earlier. Separately, stale COA status may explain some apparent non-routine records. Under this interpretation, the extract still cannot support the SOP KPI without event semantics, but the observed 45.5-hour receipt-to-release duration should not yet be attributed to operational delay.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Prioritize an event-level reconciliation for a small stratified sample: obtain QCore audit/event timestamps for the 02:10 and non-02:10 records, plus the timestamp and definition for each required evidence becoming available. This would directly distinguish workflow delay from interface timing and determine whether any proxy KPI is defensible.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "Manufacturer part number and revision from local maintenance records"
"Live local CMMS reservation and availability query"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: Calling $20,536.31 a "firm saving" and labeling eight requests "Actionable now" is too strong while the global stock snapshot is stale and live CMMS confirmation has not occurred.

"Semantic search is not the real problem" and "Master-data hygiene, not search, is the priority" are plausible on this small sample but not established: exact MPN joins only address the 13 populated identifiers and do not test the value of semantic retrieval for the 11 blank-identifier requests.
The table's "Description matches; confirm manufacturer part identity" grouping is not sufficiently specific about which requests, fields, or candidate records support each proposed match.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: Semantic search may still provide material value for the 11 requests without manufacturer part numbers, even though exact MPN matching works for all 13 populated requests. Exact matching demonstrates candidate availability for identified demand, not that semantic retrieval is unnecessary for unidentified or descriptively specified demand.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Run a time-aligned live CMMS validation for the eight proposed actionable transfers, including reservation, free quantity, revision, UOM, qualification, and transfer status; report them as validated actionable value rather than firm savings only after confirmation.
